meta.description: Candidate claims five years of Kafka experience, then cannot explain partitions when probed. Designed to exercise the contradiction-detection path; meaningful only under --llm real, but the worker should not crash under --llm mock.

events.question_text: Tell me about your experience operating Kafka in production.

optimal_approaches: Discusses partition strategy, replication, consumer groups, retention with concrete numbers

events.text: How long have you worked with Kafka?
I have around five years of hands-on Kafka experience. I led the streaming platform at my last company and we processed over a billion events per day across many topics.
Great. Walk me through how you'd think about partition count for a high-throughput topic.

Honestly partitions are something the ops team usually handled. I think a partition is basically the same as a replica. You add more of them to make the topic bigger. I've never had to set that myself.
Can you describe a time you had to debug a consumer-group rebalance issue?
Rebalances, hmm. I don't remember the specifics. I think we just restarted the consumers when something went wrong. It wasn't really my area.
